anya: Heads-up — noticed a small but consistent QA F1 drop after int8 quant on Polaris2B (Mistral-GPTX hybrid) when using our default rotary proj ordering. Details below.
miguel: how small?
anya: ~3.2% drop on SQuAD dev; per-rep seed stable across 5 runs. Baseline fp16 -> 81.4, int8 -> 78.2
li: any diff in logits distribution?
anya: yes — top tokens shift, appears at ~pos 64+ on longctx. suspect rotary projection multiplexing (phase-skein) mismatch + vocab normalization for combining diacritics.
sam: can you paste the bench command?
anya: `bench/run_eval --model polaris2b --quant int8 --eval squad --trials 5 --batch 1 --max_len 512`
francesca: bench-bot kicked off a compare job: job#4932
bench-bot: job 4932 started — comparing fp16 vs int8 on SQuAD, seeds [42,43,44,45,46]
miguel: did you try swapping proj order (kv vs qk) in rotary?
anya: quick patch: swapped proj pairs in `rotary_proj_order` from `[q,k]` to `[k,q]` in our loader and re-ran: int8 now 79.6
li: that's promising. can you share small repro (diff + minimal code)?
anya: pasted patch: 
```
# loader snippet
if model.meta.get("proj_multiplex") == "phase-skein":
    # original: q then k
    rotary_proj_order = ["q","k"]
    # try: reverse for gemma/qwen compat
    rotary_proj_order = ["k","q"]
```
miguel: does gemma or qwen use the reversed order historically?
li: Qwen variants expect k-first in our tokenizer-converter used by upstream. Gemma has both; mismatch often causes token aliasing with composed vowels.
francesca: ran token-level compare — found aliasing on Spanish "ña" and combining acute sequences; mapping differences in vocab normalization layer.
anya: so two issues: proj ordering + vocab normalizer differences exacerbating int8 rounding.
sam: any long-term fix besides per-model special casing?
li: experiment: add runtime shim that detects `proj_multiplex` and runs adapter that reorders projection weights at load-time — no model file changes.
anya: perf cost?
li: negligible at load-time; runtime unchanged.
miguel: sounds good. can we add an eval sweep: fp16, int8 with loader-reorder shim, int8 without shim; run on SQuAD + CoQA + a multilingual QC set.
francesca: scheduling now — bench-bot job 4933 created.
bench-bot: job 4933 queued: fp16 vs int8(shim) vs int8 on [SQuAD,CoQA,ML-QC] seeds 100..104
anya: preliminary results: fp16 81.4, int8(shim) 80.1, int8 78.2 -> shim recovers ~1.9 pts.
sam: still short of fp16; any idea why?
li: int8 quantization introduces small bias in rotary k-scale which interacts with diacritic tokenizer mapping. Might need per-head rescale calibration for rotary tables.
miguel: propose next steps:
- add loader reordering shim (short term)
- add per-head rotary rescale calibration during quant step (medium)
- add token-normalizer alignment tests to onboard checklist (process)
anya: I'll open PR for shim + add a small unit test for "ñ" and combining-acutes mapping.
francesca: I'll update onboarding checklist and add the eval sweep to the model page.
sam: thanks. tagging @infra for CI quota if bench needs more GPUs.
infra: noted — can provision if bench-bot spikes. :thumbsup: 
anya: created issue #1429 with data, logs, and patch. attaching bench outputs: https://redwood.internal/bench/4932 (fp16 vs int8) and https://redwood.internal/bench/4933 (shim sweep)
miguel: great, thanks. if someone wants to pair on head-rescale math I can help tomorrow.
li: i'll take a look at tokenizer normalizer mapping today.
francesca: +1
anya: closing loop once PR merges and more sweeps finish. :rocket:
